ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer to determine whether the 22:39–22:50 off-route segment (F3) was on the rider-agreed Bukit Timah Road; if it was not, refund the metered excess distance at $1.4101/km on the extra_km of that segment (RydeTAXI metered trip, RD-2) via Ryde voucher under NS-7. No account action on either profile (F17, F18).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance driven feeds the fare and any unexcused off-route km is refundable: the meter charged $34.35 for 24.36 km, i.e. $34.35 ÷ 24.36 km = $1.4101/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The trace confirms one off-route segment exists, F3, 22:39–22:50, 7.34 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.77 km, adding 4.57 km [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse that segment: no traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window, and RD-4(a) requires an incident on the replaced stretch [F15][RD-4]. The only congestion record is the Pan Island Expressway at band 2 (10–19 km/h) 22:13–22:39, which ends exactly when F3 begins and under RD-4(b) is corroborative at best and does not on its own exempt a segment [F12][F3][RD-4]. Heavy rain (18.5 mm) is not an RD-4 ground [F16][RD-4].

RD-5 consent: the driver asked at 22:35 "ok if I go round via Bukit Timah Road?" and the rider replied at 22:36 "Can lah, go ahead." — a rider message, timestamped, sent before the segment's 22:39 start, agreeing to a specifically named road [F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed adds nothing; a driver's claim is not consent, and it is not needed here [F11][RD-5]. Both advocates state the same ground — named road agreed, but no record ties the driven segment to Bukit Timah Road (no stop on that road, no message placing the car there, no road name in any fact) — so under RD-5 and G13 the scope tie is undetermined: timing alone does not prove the segment was driven on the agreed road [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. A named-road agreement whose tie to the driven segment the record cannot settle is not exempt, and this finding changes the amount, so the amount cannot be computed on this record: that is a reason to send the case to a person, not to pick a side.

Amount: the refundable head would be the extra_km of the non-exempt segment × $1.4101/km (trace formula). F3's geometry implies 4.57 km × $1.4101/km = $6.4443 → $6.44, while the fare record bills excess distance of $6.66 for 4.72 km at the same rate ($6.66 ÷ 4.72 km = $1.4110/km, the record's own stated excess); RD-2 refunds only the non-exempt segment's extra_km, and the 0.15 km difference is corridor noise not attributable to a segment, so it is not refundable [F3][F4][RD-2]. Because the segment's status is undetermined, no amount is fixed here.

Flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days and the driver's record shows 0 upheld (2 disputes, 0 upheld), so the "repeated" precondition fails and no flag_account is issued; profile facts decide nothing on their own [F18][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read F8 (a courteous route question), F9 (a short consent), F11 (driver's statement) and the rider's complaint; nothing reads as a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation, and no collision or injury is recorded (F15), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not triggered [F8][F9][F11][F15][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message at 22:36, 'Can lah, go ahead.' (F9), was sent before the 22:39 start of F3 (F3) and answers the driver's 22:35 question naming a specific road, Bukit Timah Road (F8), so the consent is a named-road authorisation under RD-5 and is timely. But RD-5 requires a record tying the segment to that road — a stop on it, a message placing the car there, a road name in a fact — and the complete, fully timestamped chat (F10) and the GPS facts carry no such tie; timing alone does not establish it (G13). Both parties state this ground, so the segment is undetermined, not exempt and not counted; the finding changes the amount and therefore goes to a person.

rejected_claims.reason: The $6.66 / 4.72 km excess-distance head and the $0.11 waiting unit cannot be awarded as requested because the only off-route segment (F3) is undetermined under RD-5/G13, not unexcused; RD-2 only refunds the extra_km of a non-exempt segment, and the record does not yet settle that [F3][F4][F5][RD-2][RD-5].

Correct that RD-4 gives no exemption — no incident on the replaced stretch (F15) and a band-2 reading that ends when F3 begins (F12) is corroborative only [F15][F12][RD-4] — but the segment is not thereby counted, since the parties agree the ground to decide is the RD-5 named-road tie [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

Accepting that the rider's 22:36 message (F9) is a valid pre-segment agreement to a named road [F8][F9][F3][RD-5] does not make F3 exempt: RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to that named road, and none does [F3][F10][RD-5].

The claim that no refund is due because the segment is consented to is rejected: consent to a named road (F9) executes an exemption only when a record ties the segment to that road (RD-5/G13), and here that tie is missing, leaving F3 undetermined [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

The no-safety-issue submission is accepted as a finding, not as a disposal of the case: SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not triggered by F8, F9, F11 or the complaint, but the case still goes to a person on the undetermined RD-5 tie [F8][F9][F11][F15][SAFE-1][SAFE-2][RD-5].
